status_rationale: Lean mapping exists and compiles (`candidates/ptx/9.3/units/xor-b16/lean/XorB16-v2.lean`) with namespace `Spec2Lean.PTX.XorB16`; this stage proposes Lean theorem obligations only with no proofs.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded scalar form `xor.b16 d, a, b;`
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b16 is in scope, with mapped state of register/predicate files, optional predicate guard, and `SourceB` allowing register/immediate while `SourceA` remains register-only per open-issue preservation in this run.

compliance_notes: No proofs are written in this stage.
The theorem set intentionally does not assert behavior for destination `Destination.bitBucket` because legality/effect remain open in the approved semantics (PTX-XORB16-SEM-008).
No semantics are imported from other units.
Theorems are phrased against definitions in this bounded artifact and are non-vacuous relative to its partial relation/function semantics.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded syntax, type, and operand shape
validation_obligations.description: Instruction form is bounded to `.b16` with optional guard and ordered fields `(d, a, b)`; destination and sources are modeled as bounded datatypes.

validation_obligations.title: 16-bit bounded value representation
validation_obligations.description: `B16` is represented as a `Fin (2 ^ 16)` value, enforcing bounded width in type.

validation_obligations.title: Minimal state and partial transition convention
validation_obligations.description: Machine state consists of register and predicate files only; executable `execXorB16` and relation `XorB16Step` are partial via missing guard/source lookups and unresolved bit-bucket destination update case.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed pre-state and instruction, the one-step relation has at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For all states `s`, instructions `i`, and states `s1 s2`, if `XorB16Step s i s1` and `XorB16Step s i s2`, then `s1 = s2`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem XorB16Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : XorB16Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : XorB16Step s i s1) (h2 : XorB16Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both executed and guard-false constructors are present in the relation, so uniqueness is a substantive claim about at-most-one reachable post-state for fixed `(s, i)`.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1 and h2; constructor mismatch on guard results is impossible after rewriting. Same-constructor cases reduce to congruence on `updateDestination` or reflexivity.

theorem_obligations.intent: Characterize executable outcomes via the relation and tie `none` to absence of a step in this bounded artifact.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) If `execXorB16 s i` is `some` executed or `some` guard-false, the corresponding `XorB16Step` holds. (b) If `XorB16Step s i s'` holds, then `execXorB16 s i` is `some` with matching state and constructor. (c) `execXorB16 s i = none` iff no `XorB16Step s i _` exists.
hypotheses: h : execXorB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')
h : execXorB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Executable-relation behavior matches branch-by-branch, and `none` is exact partiality.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: This bridges two independently defined interfaces (`execXorB16` and `XorB16Step`) and includes all branches, including partiality (`none`).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold definitions and split on `evalGuard`, source lookups, and destination update result; match each branch to the corresponding relation constructor.

theorem_obligations.intent: Under true guard and resolved sources with register destination, execution writes exactly `xorValue va vb` to that destination register.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If guard evaluates to true, `i.d = Destination.reg r`, and source reads are `va` and `vb`, then `execXorB16 s i` returns `some (ExecOutcome.executed s')` and `s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb)`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execXorB16_xor_result (s : MachineState) (i : XorB16Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B16) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va) (hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execXorB16 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (xorValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : evalSourceA s i.a = some va
hb : evalSourceB s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: There exists a deterministic executed state where destination register value equals `xorValue va vb`.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The theorem ties concrete bitwise semantics `d := a ^ b` to an explicit destination-register value in the resulting state.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use `hguard`, `ha`, `hb` to force the executed branch, then simplify `updateDestination` under `hd` and read back the destination field.

theorem_obligations.intent: Predicate registers are preserved by a one-step relation transition in this bounded model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any `XorB16Step s i s'`, every predicate register has identical value in `s` and `s'`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem XorB16Step_predicate_file_frame (s : MachineState) (i : XorB16Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : XorB16Step s i s') : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The bounded state model includes predicate files and the transition updates only value registers for register destinations, so this is a meaningful frame-property theorem.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split on relation constructor; both constructors preserve predicate file equality by direct simplification and extensionality.
theorem_obligations.proof_requires_open_question_handling: No theorem in this file relies on semantics for `Destination.bitBucket` or mandatory undefined semantics for false-guard side effects.
